answer: When signups on any day pass 3x the 30-day average, accounts made that day count as one voter on any panel until they're 60 days old. So if two of them land on the same velvet mill audit or ember kiln log check, their grades get averaged into a single vote, though each seat still pays as usual. Normal days change nothing. A farm that dumps 400 accounts in one tide gets one vote per panel out of all of them. To dodge it, it has to drip accounts in under the line, about 2x the usual daily rate, so building a big bloc takes months, not an afternoon.
